    // The world after solving row `index` once for POSITION: the normal axis only,
    // aiming at the correction speed, with no restitution and no friction. Friction
    // is deliberately absent — a fictitious tangential velocity would shear a stack
    // sideways as it settles.
    //
    // The row's NormalImpulse field is reused as the accumulator for the pseudo
    // impulse, so the clamp is on the accumulated value exactly as in the velocity
    // solve and a later row can undo an earlier row's over-push. That reuse is safe
    // because `SolvePositions` runs on a copy whose constraints it discards; only
    // the body twists survive.
    SolvePositionRow(world: RigidWorld3D, index: Integer): RigidWorld3D
    {
        var row = world.Constraints[index];
        var a = world.Bodies[row.BodyA.Value];
        var b = world.Bodies[row.BodyB.Value];
        var n = row.Normal.Vector;
        var increment = ImpulseFor(
            CorrectionSpeed(row.Penetration, world.Solver, world.TimeStep.FixedDeltaTime.Seconds),
            SeparationSpeed(a, b, row.Point, n),
            DirectionalMass(a, b, row.Point, n));
        var total = (row.NormalImpulse.Amount + increment).Max(0.0);
        var applied = total - row.NormalImpulse.Amount;
        return RigidWorld3D(
            ReplacedAt(
                ReplacedAt(world.Bodies, row.BodyA.Value, ApplyImpulse(a, n * -applied, row.Point)),
                row.BodyB.Value,
                ApplyImpulse(b, n * applied, row.Point)),
            ReplacedAt(world.Constraints, index, WithImpulses(row,
                Impulse.FromAmount(total), row.TangentImpulse, row.BitangentImpulse)),
            world.Gravity,
            world.TimeStep,
            world.Solver);
    }
